resources.string: Open link2linux on your Linux computer and keep both devices on the same network. To pair, scan the code it shows, or check that both screens show the same short code.
This phone and the computer forget each other. To connect again, you pair them again.
Keep this screen open and stay on the same network as your computer. This ends in %1$d s.
Still nothing? On your computer, choose to enter the phone\'s address, and type one of these:
On your computer, pick this phone from the list. It is listed as %1$s. This ends in %2$d s.
The last attempt did not work: %1$s
If it is not listed, type one of these addresses on the computer:
The two devices are making sure they are talking to each other.
Compare this code with the one on %1$s. Only continue if they match exactly.
%1$s says it is the computer you paired as %2$s, but it has a different key. Replace the old pairing only if you set up that computer again. If you are unsure, choose No.
This phone and the computer now trust each other.
The devices could not confirm each other. Check that you scanned the code on your own computer, then try again.
Pairing was declined, so nothing was saved.
The computer did not connect in time. Check that both devices are on the same network, then try again.
The computer was not expecting this phone. Show a new code on the computer and scan it again.
This phone or the computer cannot pair this way.
The connection dropped before pairing finished.
The phone could not wait for the computer. Check the network connection and try again.
